Suppose that the following conditions are satisfied: (i) X(θ) ≤rh↑ Y(θ), ∀θ ∈ (a, b); (ii) X(θ1) ≤rh (≥rh) X(θ2), ∀a < θ1 ≤ θ2 < b, or Y(θ1) ≤rh (≥rh) Y(θ2), ∀a < θ1 ≤ θ2 < b; (iii) Fθ(x)/Gθ(x + Δ) is increasing (decreasing) in θ ∈ (a, b), for every fixed x ∈ (l, u) and Δ ≥ 0; (iv) Θ1 ≤rh (≥hr) Θ2. Then, X(Θ1) ≤rh↑ Y(Θ2).

records.quote: Shanthikumar and Yao (1986) and Lillo et al. (2000) proved that if Xi ≤lr↑ Yi, i = 1, 2, then X1 + X2 ≤lr↑ Y1 + Y2. In addition, Hu and Zhu (2001) proved that if X1 ≤lr↑ Y1 and X2 ≤lr↑ (respectively, ≤hr↑ and ≤rh↑) Y2, then X1 + X2 ≤lr↑ (respectively, ≤hr↑ and ≤rh↑) Y1 + Y2. ... However, using the general result stated in Lemma 2.7, the assertion follows in a straight-forward manner. ... it is easy to see that hypotheses of the theorem are satisfied and hence, X1 + X2 ≤lr↑ (respectively, ≤hr↑ and ≤rh↑) Y1 + Y2.
